item.title: Tests on 8 frozen Inca mummies sacrificed show they had chewed coca leaves and had drunk alcohol
item.description: A remarkable archaeological find has revealed eight frozen mummies of children from the Inca Empire, believed to have been sacrificed. Analysis of their hair and nails showed they've ingested coca and alcohol, hinting at a diversity of ritual practices based on local customs. Notably, one mummy, Juanita, contained harmine traces, suggesting specialized ritualistic preparations. This research unveils a rich tapestry of ancient cultural traditions and ceremonies. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Ancient Maya cities used red pigment in temples; study finds it left mercury in lakes for centuries
item.description: Ancient Maya civilization used a red pigment made of mercury-rich cinnabar for decoration and rituals. This practice led to significant mercury contamination of nearby lakes and ecosystems. Research indicates that rising mercury levels impacted aquatic organisms and may have affected human health. Previous studies have also shown similar contamination at various Maya sites, raising concerns about widespread environmental impact. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
